items.stem: In which work by Callimachus does The poet celebrant appear as speaker who calls the god and guides the hymn?
items.explanation: The poet celebrant (The speaker who calls the god and guides the hymn) is a prominent character in Callimachus's Hymns.

items.title: Quiz Q#221 · Callimachus
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Keep your Muse slender."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Callimachus's Hymns (3rd century BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#222 · Callimachus
items.stem: Which collection of six learned hexameter poems by Callimachus celebrates various Olympian deities (such as Zeus, Apollo, Artemis, and Delos) with exquisite mythological erudition?
items.explanation: Callimachus's Hymns represent the pinnacle of Hellenistic court poetry, blending religious form with artistic refinement.

items.title: Quiz Q#223 · Apollonius of Rhodes

items.explanation: Jason (Leader of the Argonauts, sent to bring back the Golden Fleece) is a prominent character in Apollonius of Rhodes's Argonautica.

items.title: Quiz Q#224 · Apollonius of Rhodes
items.meta: Ancient & Classical World · Apollonius of Rhodes
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Beginning with thee, O Phoebus."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Apollonius of Rhodes's Argonautica (3rd century BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#225 · Apollonius of Rhodes
items.meta: Ancient & Classical World · Apollonius of Rhodes
items.stem: Which Hellenistic epic poem in four books recounts Jason and the Argonauts' perilous voyage to Colchis to retrieve the Golden Fleece, featuring Medea's passionate love?
items.explanation: Apollonius of Rhodes's Argonautica (3rd century BCE) is the only surviving Hellenistic epic, famous for its psychological depiction of Medea's romantic awakening.

items.title: Quiz Q#226 · Terence
items.stem: In which work by Terence does the character 'Pamphilus (A young Athenian who loves Glycerium and fears his father's wedding plan)' appear?
items.explanation: Pamphilus (A young Athenian who loves Glycerium and fears his father's wedding plan) is a central character in Terence's Andria (166 BCE).

items.stem: Which first comedy by Terence, produced in 166 BCE and based on plays by Menander, tells the story of Pamphilus whose love for the maid Glycerium is complicated by his father's arranged marriage plans?
items.explanation: Terence's Andria ('The Girl from Andros', 166 BCE) marked his debut on the Roman stage, praised for elegant Latinity and moral sensitivity.

items.title: Quiz Q#228 · Terence
items.stem: In which work by Terence does Chaerea appear as A young man who disguises himself as the eunuch Dorus?
items.explanation: Chaerea (A young man who disguises himself as the eunuch Dorus) is a prominent character in Terence's The Eunuch.

items.title: Quiz Q#229 · Terence
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus freezes."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Terence's The Eunuch (161 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#230 · Terence
items.stem: Which most financially successful comedy by Terence, staged at the Megalensian Games in 161 BCE, depicts young Chaerea disguising himself as a eunuch to gain access to his beloved Pamphila?
items.explanation: Terence's The Eunuch (161 BCE) was extraordinarily popular in Rome, earning an unprecedented encore and payment.

items.title: Quiz Q#231 · Terence
items.stem: In which work by Terence does Demea appear as strict country father of Aeschinus and Ctesipho?
items.explanation: Demea (The strict country father of Aeschinus and Ctesipho) is a prominent character in Terence's The Brothers.

items.title: Quiz Q#232 · Terence
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"I did it to show you."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Terence's The Brothers (160 BCE).

items.stem: Which final play by Terence (Adelphoe), staged in 160 BCE, contrasts the differing child-rearing philosophies of two brothers—the stern country father Demea and the lenient urban uncle Micio?
items.explanation: Terence's The Brothers (160 BCE) is a thoughtful social comedy analyzing authoritarian versus permissive parenting.

items.title: Quiz Q#234 · Cicero

items.explanation: Lucius Licinius Crassus (A great Roman orator who defends a widely educated speaker) is a prominent character in Cicero's De Oratore.

items.title: Quiz Q#235 · Cicero

items.title: Quiz Q#236 · Cicero
items.stem: Which three-book rhetorical dialogue by Cicero, set in 91 BCE, features the famous speakers Crassus and Antonius debating whether the ideal orator requires broad philosophical culture or mere technical training?
items.explanation: Cicero's De Oratore (55 BCE) presents his humanist vision of the perfect orator as an educated philosopher-statesman.

items.title: Quiz Q#237 · Cicero
items.stem: In which work by Cicero does the character 'Scipio Aemilianus (The wise leader who explains Rome's constitution and tells the dream)' appear?
items.explanation: Scipio Aemilianus (The wise leader who explains Rome's constitution and tells the dream) is a central character in Cicero's De Republica (51 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#238 · Cicero
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Virtue should lead you to true glory."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Cicero's De Republica (51 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#239 · Cicero
items.stem: In which philosophical dialogue by Cicero on political theory and the ideal commonwealth does the famous concluding section, 'The Dream of Scipio' (Somnium Scipionis), occur?
items.explanation: Cicero's De Republica (51 BCE) examines constitutional theory, ending with the 'Dream of Scipio' which describes the heavenly reward awaiting virtuous statesmen.

items.title: Quiz Q#240 · Cicero
items.stem: In which work by Cicero does Cicero appear as main speaker, who surveys Roman orators and defends his style?
items.explanation: Cicero (The main speaker, who surveys Roman orators and defends his style) is a prominent character in Cicero's Brutus.

items.title: Quiz Q#241 · Cicero
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Many good orators have fled Rome."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Cicero's Brutus (46 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#242 · Cicero
items.stem: Which work by Cicero, composed in 46 BCE and framed as a dialogue with Atticus and Brutus, provides the first comprehensive critical history of Roman eloquence and orators?
items.explanation: Cicero's Brutus (46 BCE) surveys over two hundred Roman orators, defending his own rhythmic, full-blooded rhetorical style against the strict Atticists.

items.title: Quiz Q#243 · Cicero
items.stem: In which work by Cicero does Cicero appear as writer, giving moral advice in the form of a letter?
items.explanation: Cicero (The writer, giving moral advice in the form of a letter) is a prominent character in Cicero's De Officiis.

items.title: Quiz Q#244 · Cicero
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"We are not born for ourselves alone."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Cicero's De Officiis (44 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#245 · Cicero
items.stem: Which final moral and philosophical treatise by Cicero, written as an extended letter of advice to his son Marcus in 44 BCE, discusses moral goodness (*honestum*), expediency (*utile*), and the duties of public life?
items.explanation: Cicero's De Officiis ('On Duties', 44 BCE) exerted immense influence on Renaissance humanism and Christian ethics.

items.title: Quiz Q#246 · Virgil
items.stem: In which work by Virgil does Tityrus appear as A shepherd who keeps his land after a visit to Rome?
items.explanation: Tityrus (A shepherd who keeps his land after a visit to Rome) is a prominent character in Virgil's Eclogues.

items.title: Quiz Q#247 · Virgil
items.stem: Which collection of ten pastoral poems by Virgil, composed between 42 and 39 BCE and modeled on Theocritus, includes the famous 'Messianic Eclogue' (Eclogue IV) predicting a golden age?
items.explanation: Virgil's Eclogues (or Bucolics, c. 39 BCE) established the pastoral mode in Latin literature, celebrated for political allegory and lush musicality.

items.title: Quiz Q#248 · Virgil
items.stem: In which work by Virgil does Aeneas appear as A Trojan prince destined to begin the Roman line?
items.explanation: Aeneas (A Trojan prince destined to begin the Roman line) is a prominent character in Virgil's Aeneid.

items.title: Quiz Q#249 · Virgil
items.stem:
Who is the author of the work containing the following line?
"Arms and the man I sing."
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Virgil's Aeneid (after 19 BCE).

items.title: Quiz Q#250 · Virgil
items.stem: Which national Roman epic in twelve books of dactylic hexameter recounts the destined journey of the Trojan prince Aeneas to Italy to found the race that would build Rome?
items.explanation: Virgil's Aeneid (29–19 BCE) is Rome's definitive epic, exploring divine duty (*pietas*), tragic sacrifice, and the imperial destiny of Augustus Caesar.
